units.title: Introduction
units.role: Problem statement: presence + immersion are conflated and imprecise. Announces the Player Involvement Model (PIM) and incorporation as the synthetic alternative.

units.title: Games Beyond Games
internal_section_headings: (plus subsections — full structure to verify in Phase 1)
units.role: Wittgensteinian family-resemblance approach to defining games; surveys the three traditional analytic axes (formal / experiential / sociocultural); positions the book on the experiential axis while drawing on the other two.

units.title: Immersion
units.role: Literature review and critique of immersion + presence; identifies four conceptual challenges the rest of the book addresses. Densest citation chapter. Heidegger cited here (p.21) — only Heidegger reference in the volume (Question Concerning Technology, 1977/1993).

units.title: The Player Involvement Model
units.role: CENTRAL CHAPTER — introduces the 6-dimensional model + macro/micro temporal-phase distinction. Builds on three years of qualitative research (WoW + Planetside; 25 in-depth interviews + focus groups). Methodological transparency: explicitly names T. L. Taylor (2006), Steinkuehler (2005), Klastrup (2004) as qualitative-virtual-worlds precedents.

units.title: Kinesthetic Involvement
internal_section_headings: (micro-phase subsections to verify — Calleja cites Murray + Schott on agency)
units.role: Dimension 1 — control, movement, agency. Engages Murray (1998) and Schott (2006) on agency.

units.title: Spatial Involvement
internal_section_headings: (further subsections to verify — Calleja cites Aarseth 2005 on labyrinthine space)
units.role: Dimension 2 — virtual-environment habitation, exploration, navigation; cites Aarseth (2005) on labyrinthine spatial structures and 'open landscape' environments.

units.title: Shared Involvement
internal_section_headings: Macro Phase: Socializing in Game Worlds
(further subsections — Oldenburg 'third spaces'; Steinkuehler + Williams cited)
units.role: Dimension 3 — social co-presence (NOT 'Share' — verify TOC). Engages LAN-party history, Steinkuehler + Williams on third-place sociality, Oldenburg.

units.title: Narrative Involvement
internal_section_headings: (further subsections — narratology engagement: Chatman, Genette, Prince; Marie-Laure Ryan on speech-act narrative)
units.role: Dimension 4 — scripted-narrative + alterbiography (emergent narrative). Engages classical narratology (Chatman, Genette, Prince) via Ryan's critique; takes up Juul-vs-Aarseth narratology debate without endorsing either pole.

units.title: Affective Involvement
internal_section_headings: (named subsections to verify — Bryant + Davies, Grodal cited; 'excitatory homeostasis' from media psychology)
units.role: Dimension 5 — emotion in gameplay; uses media-psychology 'excitatory homeostasis'; cites Bryant + Davies (2006) and Grodal (2000). Note: SHORTEST dimension chapter (12 pp.) — much shorter than the other five; possibly reflects Calleja's least-developed dimension at the time of writing.

units.title: Ludic Involvement
internal_section_headings: (further subsections — Caillois paidia/ludus; Salen+Zimmerman; Juul on magic circle)
units.role: Dimension 6 — rules, goals, choices, agency. Engages Caillois (1962) paidia/ludus distinction; Salen+Zimmerman (2003); Juul (2005) on magic circle.

units.title: From Immersion to Incorporation
internal_section_headings: (unnamed opening — recaps 4 conceptual challenges from Ch.2)
(further subsections to verify in Phase 1; Lakoff+Johnson 'experiential gestalts' invoked; Damasio cited)
units.role: TITULAR SYNTHESIS CHAPTER — argues incorporation displaces immersion/presence as primary frame. Invokes Lakoff+Johnson (2003) experientialist ontology + Damasio (2000) on consciousness. Emphasizes the 'metaphor of habitation' grounded in everyday lived experience.

units.title: Conclusion
units.role: Methodological reflection (invokes Genette's Narrative Discourse + Narrative Discourse Revisited as model-revision exemplar); positions the volume as a 'first considered step' in structural modeling of player involvement; gestures toward poststructural successor.

units.title: Appendix: A Tale of Two Worlds
internal_section_headings: (further subsections to verify in Phase 1 — covers WoW + Planetside genre and spatial design)
units.role: Full-unit treatment (per plan v3). Provides WoW + Planetside genre + topography profiles for readers unfamiliar with MMOGs. Note: figures here are numbered 12.1, 12.2 — internal-chapter numbering treats the Appendix as Chapter 12.

figure_inventory.notes: No figures in Ch.1, Intro, Conclusion. Heaviest figure load in Ch.4 (Kinesthetic) and Ch.5 (Spatial) — both dimensions where visual referents are central.

burke.verdict: ABSENT. Dissertation's Burke pentad + consubstantiation augmentation (Layer B) is wholly CREATIVE / ANTICIPATORY, not exegetical. Burke does not appear in Calleja's intellectual horizon at the time of writing.
burke.implication: All burke_pentad_mapping entries in PIM Operationalization Manual Section E must carry provenance='anticipatory-projection (dissertation)'.

heidegger.sole_reference: Heidegger, Martin. 1993 [1977]. The Question Concerning Technology and Other Essays. New York: Harper & Row.
heidegger.context: Cited once, in Ch.2 Immersion at p.21, in a brief discussion of interpretive comportment ('critically removed and we must actively think about what we are doing'). No engagement with Being and Time, Dasein, In-der-Welt-sein, zuhanden, or any phenomenological-ontological apparatus.
heidegger.verdict: PRESENT BUT MINIMAL. Calleja's Heidegger is the late-Heidegger of technology critique, not the SZ-era Heidegger of Dasein/Zuhandenheit. Dissertation's BCAP-grounded Heidegger augmentation (Layer A) remains CREATIVE relative to Calleja's text.
heidegger.implication: awaits-ontological-grounding-in edges to Heidegger BCAP corpus index must carry provenance='anticipatory-projection (dissertation)'.

aristotle.verdict: ABSENT. Dissertation's Aristotelian augmentation (Layer A) is wholly CREATIVE. Calleja's text contains zero Aristotelian or classical-rhetorical vocabulary.
aristotle.implication: All Phantasia-Cluster / Bowin-AMT bridges are anticipatory.

merleau_ponty.verdict: ABSENT. Despite explicit kinesthetic/spatial/affective thematics that obviously invite phenomenological treatment, Calleja does not draw on Merleau-Ponty. The phenomenological vocabulary in IG-10 (e.g., 'experiential gestalts') comes via Lakoff+Johnson (2003) and Damasio (2000), not via classical phenomenology.

gibson.verdict: CRITICAL FINDING — GIBSON ABSENT, AFFORDANCE GENERIC. Calleja uses 'affordance' / 'affordances' 11 times across the book WITHOUT attributing the term to J. J. Gibson, without citing Gibson, and without using the word 'ecological'. Gibson does not appear in references and does not appear in the index. The Gibson-as-implicit-Uexküll-bridge hypothesis (plan v3 §5 Phase 0) is FALSIFIED.
gibson.implication: Layer C (Uexküll) is NOT doubly-anchored via Gibson. It must be repositioned as a SINGLY-ANCHORED anticipatory projection. The Gibson pipeline forward-reference (Manual Section E gibson_pipeline_status) remains valid as a future bridge but cannot be claimed as a mediated bridge already present in Calleja. This is consequential for the manual's 'Gibson-as-the-implicit-Uexküll-bridge' framing in Section E — that subsection should be rewritten to flag that Calleja's affordance-talk is theoretically thin and that Gibson grounding will have to come from the Gibson pipeline itself, not from Calleja.

uexkull.verdict: ABSENT. Dissertation's Uexküll augmentation (Layer C) is wholly CREATIVE. Calleja's text contains zero biosemiotic vocabulary.

ONE Heidegger (Question Concerning Technology only, single citation at p.21). cross_pipeline_bridge_candidates.rationale: Calleja's Ch.5 Spatial Involvement repeatedly invokes 'mental simulation', cognitive maps of game worlds, and projection of imagination into represented landscapes — all candidate phantasia-operations. Ch.10 invokes Lakoff+Johnson 'experiential gestalts' which parallels imagistic-cognitive phantasia. ANTICIPATORY — Calleja never uses 'phantasia'.

Calleja's Ch.8 Affective Involvement engages emotion-in-gameplay via media psychology (Grodal, Bryant+Davies). Gross's situated-emotion + Berlant cruel-optimism frame would significantly extend Calleja's relatively thin affective chapter. Note: Calleja does NOT cite Gibson, so the Gross-Calleja bridge cannot be anchored via shared-Gibson affordance theory as v3 plan anticipated.

cross_pipeline_bridge_candidates.pipeline: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy (BCAP)
cross_pipeline_bridge_candidates.rationale: Calleja's macro/micro temporal-phase distinction (Ch.3) is the strongest pre-augmentation bridge to phenomenological time-analysis. Off-line macro involvement = anticipatory/retentional structure of player-being toward the game; micro = moment-to-moment ekstatic engagement. BCAP's analyses of kairos and temporality would deepen this. ANTICIPATORY — Calleja's only Heidegger cite is Question Concerning Technology (1977/1993) for technological comportment, not for time-phenomenology.
Bridge to micro-phase kinesthetic and ludic involvement via aisthesis-kinesis and continuous-motion analysis. ANTICIPATORY.

cross_pipeline_bridge_candidates.pipeline: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans
cross_pipeline_bridge_candidates.rationale: Strongest Layer C candidate. Spatial involvement (Ch.5) maps to Umwelt; Kinesthetic (Ch.4) maps to Funktionskreis; Affective (Ch.8) maps to Merktone/Wirktone. CRITICAL ADJUSTMENT FROM PLAN v3: the Gibson-via-affordance mediation hypothesis is FALSIFIED (see cite_check.gibson) — Calleja uses 'affordance' generically without Gibson attribution. Layer C must be repositioned as singly-anchored anticipatory projection, NOT as doubly-anchored mediated bridge.
cross_pipeline_bridge_candidates.adjustment_note: Plan v3 Section 5 Phase 0 + Manual Section E gibson_pipeline_status framing must be updated: Calleja's 11 'affordance' uses do NOT establish a Gibson bridge; thus the Uexkull-via-Gibson-via-Calleja chain does not exist. The forward-reference to a future Gibson pipeline as the proper bridge anchor remains valid.

cross_pipeline_bridge_candidates.rationale: Every PIM dimension is a candidate operationalizable construct for the dissertation's empirical adaptation chapter. The Appendix's WoW + Planetside case profiles supply the methodological seed.

cross_pipeline_bridge_candidates.pipeline: Kenneth Burke (1945 Grammar of Motives + Hawhee 2009 Moving Bodies anchor)
cross_pipeline_bridge_candidates.rationale: Pentad mapping per dimension (Kinesthetic->Agency, Spatial->Scene, Shared->Agent+ratio, Narrative->Act+Purpose, Affective->Attitude, Ludic->Purpose+Act); consubstantiation as candidate theoretical complement to incorporation. ANTICIPATORY — Burke is wholly absent from Calleja's text.
